title: Preserve class-typed driver denials in durable fault records
description: HIGH-risk backend observability-only repair vs BASE 709f71a9e9ebb78adc3e813d0da3734364d7b3b3. A shared DriverDenial class and closed DRIVER_FAULT_LABELS module removes the driver/scheduler import cycle while preserving the driver public re-export. faultCode now recognizes only actual DriverDenial instances with allowlisted label and matching FAIL_CLOSED_<label> code prior to generic IntegrityError fallback. Non-driver IntegrityError and forged/unknown/tampered inputs remain generic; no raw error messages persisted. Existing PASS_FAULT, SETTLE_FAULT, skipped/tick results consume faultCode; recordDenial already saves e.label and quarantine sanitizes. Pure mapping/forgery tests plus C04/C29 integration: the mid-pass revoke/pause control calls now carry the current policy_version (previously they threw FAIL_CLOSED_POLICY_VERSION_CONFLICT before gate() ran, so the scenario never exercised DriverDenial) — C04 now proves a real mid-pass DriverDenial(DRIVER_AUTHORITY_LOST) persists into last_result.fault and the QUARANTINED blocked_reason, and that the canonical observe path reaps the stale lease as INVALIDATED after the worker's release is denied. No lease, heartbeat, retry, scheduler behavior or UI changes. Live demo repro is not available in this environment. npm verify:change and full suite have NOT run in this connector-only environment; hand off to local Devin for mandatory READY_FOR_INDEPENDENT_AUDIT and independent audit. No merge.
